header:
Date: 2025-04-22
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~63 mins
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Rao (Redwood SE); Maya Patel (Voltiva Head of ML); Jon Ruiz (Voltiva SRE); Sophie Lane (Voltiva Product); Chris Park (Voltiva Security)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — Alex from Redwood, AE. Priya our solutions engineer will walk through the Optimize console and show how we do precision orchestration, and then leave time for security and deployment questions.
[00:22] Maya Patel: Hi all, Maya here, thanks. We're particularly interested in quality for triage tasks in our EHR routing system, but latency is also critical for our in-clinic workflows.
[00:39] Priya Rao: Great — quick agenda. we'll demo an Optimize sandbox, show INT8 vs FP8 profiles, talk about fallback rules and rollout strategies, then discuss security/KMS/VPC concerns. sound good?
[00:56] Jon Ruiz: Sounds good. also want to know about telemetry and token-level cost breakdowns.
[01:05] Alex Chen: Yep we'll hit observability — cost per token, per-model, per-route, and how the console surfaces regressions.
[01:17] Sophie Lane: quick question, are you supporting on-prem for compliance reasons? we may need a private deployment.
[01:24] Priya Rao: Yes, Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane. we can run the optimizer and runtime inside your VPC or on-prem appliance. there's some nuance with KMS/HSM integration for key wraps, which we'll cover.
[01:42] Chris Park: For security we'll need SOC2 artifacts, rotation policy, and audit logs retention. also SSO/SAML.
[01:50] Alex Chen: We'll share SOC2 + KMS doc after the call. noted.
[02:00] [Demo begins] Priya Rao: Ok screen share — Optimize console, Sandbox: 'voltiva-ehr-sandbox'. first panel shows model candidates and profiling metrics — p95 latency, 90th token throughput, and a fidelity score we compute from eval prompts.
[02:23] Priya Rao: Here i have the same model (open-weight-7b) with three precision profiles: baseline FP16, INT8 profile A, FP8 profile B. notice baseline latency ~128ms p95 for our 64-token median, INT8 is ~82ms, FP8 is ~95ms in this run.
[02:43] Maya Patel: those deltas look promising, what's the expected quality hit for our triage intent classification?
[02:50] Priya Rao: we run a fidelity eval set — for your triage prompts i pulled a subset. baseline EM/accuracy 92.4%, INT8 drops to 90.1% (approximately), FP8 91.6%. these numbers vary by prompt type.
[03:10] Jon Ruiz: is that eval done with your KV cache warming? our workload often has long prefixes.
[03:18] Priya Rao: good call — these runs used cold start, no KV cache. when warmed, latency improves substantially and token-level cost decreases due to cached KV. we can provision a warm-run benchmark in the sandbox.
[03:32] Alex Chen: also worth noting the console exposes a per-route fallback rule: if quality drops below X or latency spike >Y, route to baseline FP16 or fallback model variant.
[03:46] Sophie Lane: can we set a SLO that prefers lower cost up to a tolerance? like 1.5% quality loss is acceptable if latency gains > 20%?
[03:55] Priya Rao: yes that's the 'precision orchestration policy' — you express constraints (max quality delta, min latency improvement) and Optimize will recommend a profile and rollout fraction.
[04:08] [00:04:08] Priya Rao: switching to the heatmap view — shows fidelity degradation per prompt bucket. here's one tricky bucket: medication name recognition. INT8 showed higher substitution errors for rare drug tokens. FP8 preserved those better.
[04:30] Maya Patel: oh that's important, we can't confuse drug names. what's the rollback path?
[04:36] Priya Rao: automatic rollback rule included: if regression rate for a tag exceeds threshold for X minutes, traffic is shifted back over 2 mins and alerts trigger. you can also pin routes to prevent rollout.
[04:52] Alex Chen: and you can attach canary tests that run enriched evals in production traffic — small percentage of real traffic flows into a canary profile for more representative metrics.
[05:07] Jon Ruiz: On the infra side, if we go private, how does autoscaling work for these precision profiles? do we need separate pools?
[05:15] Priya Rao: we recommend a couple of variant pools: a high-fidelity FP16 pool and a low-cost quantized pool. the runtime's smart routing can shift by policy. autoscaler treats each pool like a node group.
[05:29] Priya Rao: Note some quantized kernels have different memory/latency characteristics, so we advise capacity headroom for tail loads.
[05:40] Alex Chen: Pricing model: you pay per-token but Optimize will show estimated cost delta for a rollout. it simulates 30-day spend based on observed token distributions.
[05:53] Sophie Lane: Do you support mixed precision per-request? e.g., request critical tokens in high precision?
[05:59] Priya Rao: Not per-token inside one call yet. However we do support per-route and adaptive fallback for later tokens using streaming policies. mixed token bitwidth is on the roadmap.
[06:13] [00:06:13] Priya Rao: Now i'll show a live microbench. running the three profiles against a set of 200 sample prompts (their sample set) — starting INT8 run...
[06:28] (typing sounds)
[06:31] Priya Rao: INT8 run complete: average latency 78ms, 1.9% accuracy drop on intent labels, cost estimate down by ~42%.
[06:43] Priya Rao: FP8 run: average latency 92ms, 0.6% accuracy drop, cost estimate down by ~31%. baseline FP16: 130ms average.
[06:58] Maya Patel: interesting. for the triage classifier we'd probably accept 0.5-1% drop but not 2%. so FP8 looks like the sweet spot.
[07:09] Priya Rao: Exactly. that's why the console suggests FP8 for tag 'triage-intent' and INT8 for 'entailment-check' where tokens are shorter and cost sensitivity is higher.
[07:22] Jon Ruiz: How do you measure hallucination differences? we need to ensure FP8 doesn't hallucinate medical content more.
[07:30] Priya Rao: We run targeted hallucination tests — specialized prompts and reference answers. For this dataset FP8 showed a tiny uptick in hallucination-only on long-generation tasks, but for classification it's negligible. we'll share raw eval samples.
[07:46] Alex Chen: also the console surfaces example-level diffs so reviewers can see specific cases where outputs diverge. good for compliance reviews.
[07:55] [00:07:55] Sophie Lane: Regarding deployments, if we want a phased pilot — what does the onboarding look like?
[08:02] Alex Chen: typical pilot: 1) share sample queries & SLOs, 2) Redwood sets up sandbox with your dataset and two quant profiles, 3) run a 1–2 week microbench and fidelity analysis, 4) adjust profiles and run canary, 5) schedule rollout. expect ~2–4 weeks to pilot depending on approvals.
[08:21] Maya Patel: what's the minimum committed capacity for dedicated GPUs?
[08:25] Priya Rao: depends on model size and throughput; for 7B models typical reserved pool starts at 4 GPUs for production. Dedicated pricing and burst options are in the contract.
[08:36] Chris Park: back to security — how do we integrate KMS? are keys stored in our HSM?
[08:43] Priya Rao: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. keys can be stored on your HSM and we use key-encryption-keys for model stores and logs. we also provide audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 exports.
[08:59] Chris Park: retention windows for logs? we need 1 year plus for some audit trails.
[09:05] Alex Chen: configurable. we'll include that in the security pack.
[09:12] [00:09:12] Priya Rao: back to the console — here's the experiment builder. you can configure a rollout: percent traffic, check windows, thresholds, and per-tag tolerance. I'm creating an experiment now: FP8 rollout for 'triage-intent' at 10% traffic with 1.0% max accuracy delta, 10% min latency improvement.
[09:37] Priya Rao: The dashboard shows preliminary risk score and affected endpoints. it's also surfaced to the incidents feed so SREs can subscribe.
[09:46] Jon Ruiz: What about telemetry volume — will we be taxed on telemetry or is it included?
[09:51] Alex Chen: Basic telemetry is included; extended retention and high-granularity traces are an add-on. we'll call out costs in the pricing sheet.
[09:59] Priya Rao: i'm switching to the fallback matrix tab — this is where you define when to fallback to FP16, to another model, or to batch requests. fallback rules can be real-time. there's also an emergency switch to pin everything back to baseline.
[10:16] Maya Patel: In the heatmap you showed, some rare-token buckets failed. can we configure targeted exceptions — like if a prompt contains regex for drug names, always route to FP16?
[10:27] Priya Rao: yes you can add request-level routing rules based on header tags, regex matches, or metadata. that's a common pattern for legal/medical tokens.
[10:38] Alex Chen: Also, the Optimize console can integrate with your feature store to annotate traffic with clinical risk tags to guide routing.
[10:48] [00:10:48] Sophie Lane: quick math question — if we move 60% of traffic to FP8 and 40% stays in FP16, with current numbers, what's the cost delta?
[10:58] Priya Rao: Rough calc from sandbox: FP8 cost is ~0.69x baseline, INT8 0.58x. So a 60/40 split yields ~0.876x cost vs baseline, about 12.4% reduction. console gives an exact projection.
[11:14] Jon Ruiz: Are there any model architecture gotchas — like attention layout that breaks quant kernels?
[11:20] Priya Rao: some custom ops and fused attention kernels can be less quant-friendly. during onboarding we run model-compat checks and may recommend a model variant or small code-path changes.
[11:31] Alex Chen: Competitors typically offer quantization but not the orchestration layer + rollback automation; some of them require you to manage canaries manually.
[11:41] Maya Patel: how deterministic are the quality deltas? we don't want surprise regressions post-rollout.
[11:48] Priya Rao: there is variance; Optimize reports confidence intervals and runs multiple seeds. we also recommend a conservatively small initial canary and ramp.
[11:59] [00:11:59] Priya Rao: i'm going to show the report export — CSV of diffs, per-example outputs, token-level timings, and a cost simulation. you can attach that to your compliance review.
[12:15] Chris Park: can the export be pulled automatically into our compliance pipeline?
[12:21] Priya Rao: yes via API or S3 export. we'll provide a sample Terraform module for S3 ingestion.
[12:31] Sophie Lane: what's the expected timeline to get the sandbox up once you have our sample prompts?
[12:36] Alex Chen: Priya typically needs 3 business days to provision a sandbox and run initial microbenches.
[12:45] Maya Patel: ok we'll aim to share the dataset by Friday.
[12:49] [00:12:49] Priya Rao: quick note on telemetry: we capture per-token latencies and per-request fidelity scores. some customers route detailed traces to their own observability to keep PII out of Redwood logs.
[13:02] Jon Ruiz: in private mode, where do logs land? directly to our S3?
[13:07] Priya Rao: yes, customers can control log sinks — S3, Splunk, Datadog. logs can be encrypted with customer keys.
[13:17] Alex Chen: time check — ~50 minutes left for deeper technical questions if you want to go into kernel-level differences.
[13:26] Maya Patel: yes let's dive a bit — which FP8 format are you using? e4m or some custom?
[13:31] Priya Rao: We use an 8-bit floating with an exponent bias similar to bfloat variant tuned for inference kernels — our runtime picks best kernel per hardware. some GPUs/DPUs have optimized FP8 paths; others emulate.
[13:48] Jon Ruiz: any fallback perf penalty when switching mid-request?
[13:52] Priya Rao: switching mid-request is not supported; fallbacks happen at request routing granularity. there's a small handover window during rollout but not per-token switching.
[14:03] [00:14:03] Priya Rao: i'll show kernel selection charts — here the runtime logs show which kernel was used, memory usage, and expected quant error. it's helpful for debugging regressions.
[14:18] Maya Patel: do you keep a lineage of which profile was used for each historical request for audit?
[14:24] Priya Rao: yes, every request's metadata includes profile id, model-version, and runtime kernel id. that's part of the audit log.
[14:34] Chris Park: how do you handle PII? we can't have PHI leave our region.
[14:40] Alex Chen: Redwood Private can be deployed in-region with egress controls. for hosted customers we support data retention controls and option to not persist raw prompts. we'll include region residency options in the security pack.
[14:56] [00:14:56] Sophie Lane: if we want to start with a low-risk scope, what do you recommend?
[15:01] Priya Rao: start with non-critical routes: autocomplete, help center answers, then move to triage-intent once comfortable. run canaries and use regex routing for sensitive tokens.
[15:15] Maya Patel: good plan. any known failure modes we should watch for?
[15:20] Priya Rao: rare-token degradation, long-tail numeric handling, and sometimes divergence in temperature-sensitive generations. console flags those automatically.
[15:33] [00:15:33] Alex Chen: ok let's surface next steps: we'll send the security pack, Priya will spin up the sandbox after we get sample prompts, and we'll schedule pilot kickoff for early May.
[15:45] Maya Patel: thanks — quick ask, can you include a sample contract appendix for dedicated? Sophie will review.
[15:52] Alex Chen: yes will include a sample appendix and price bands.
[15:57] Jon Ruiz: one last technical — can we run the microbench against our internal hardware for a true apples-to-apples?
[16:03] Priya Rao: yes we offer a benchmarking harness you can run internally; we can also run Redwood-managed microbench and compare results.
[16:12] [00:16:12] Alex Chen: cool. wrapping up — any other blockers?
[16:16] Maya Patel: none on my side. we'll share sample prompts and SLOs.
[16:21] Chris Park: awaiting SOC2 docs.
[16:24] Alex Chen: noted. we'll follow up with the pack and a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[16:30] [00:16:30] (call winds down, brief chatter)
[17:02] [00:17:02] Speaker 1: thank you all, bye.
[17:10] [END] Note: some proper nouns in this transcript may be misrecognized (e.g., model variant names and kernel identifiers). raw audio attached in Fireflies export.
